rationale: B wins because it keeps three real shapes and does not try to make one Rivian announcement carry an industry verdict. A's kept angle, "Every new Rivian stall will carry both plugs — the connector fight is over," is the kind of confident overreach that gets a reporter to check out. B's "Rivian adds Tesla-style plugs and opens its network with no automaker partner in sight" keeps the same infrastructure story inside the facts and asks for the missing proof instead of pretending it has it.
gaps_in_A: "the connector fight is over" is not in the update and overstates one company's dual-plug decision as an industry conclusion.
"joining the small set of automaker-owned networks" imports outside market context without evidence from the supplied facts.
Angle 1 and Angle 4 overlap on network access, NACS, and no-partner positioning; the fourth angle needed a cleaner standards peg or should have been folded into the infrastructure angle.
"competing for the same drivers rather than negotiating with their manufacturers" turns "no partnership announced" into a strategic motive the update does not prove.
gaps_in_B: "whether opening the network dilutes a perk existing owners bought into" is a fair question, but it needs care; the update does not say Rivian marketed exclusivity as a paid owner benefit.
"under public-market scrutiny for losses" is directionally fair from "publicly traded and not yet profitable," but it is still phrased as market context the update itself does not document.
